newsitem.title: FRANCE: BA's French airline workers occupy offices.
newsitem.headline: BA's French airline workers occupy offices.

text.p: About 100 cockpit crew from British Airways' French subsidiaries TAT and Air Liberte occupied the airlines' Paris airport offices on Friday and vowed to remain until managing director Marc Rochet talked to them.

"Marc Rochet is locked in his office. He has told union representatives that he will not negotiate until everyone has left the premises except the union negotiators. But our members do not want to leave. We are going to remain here as long as it takes," union leader Jean Immediato told Reuters by telephone.
A French court in suburban Paris will rule on April 25 on a challenge to a British Airways move to manage TAT and Air Liberte as a joint unit and eventually to merge the two carriers.
The BA cost-cutting moves, aimed at bringing the carriers to profitability, have prompted a strike by TAT and Air Liberte cockpit crews that was expected to enter its 11th day on Saturday.
In several similar labour-management confrontations in recent months, French unions have held managers in their offices for days on end to pressure companies to call off closures or planned job cuts.
Due to the continuing strikes, Air Liberte said it would fly just 72 percent of its scheduled flights on Saturday while TAT said it would offer just 70 percent of its scheduled flights.
